newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi white sugar to reach market this month.
newsitem.headline: Saudi white sugar to reach market this month.

text.p: The first locally refined sugar will reach Saudi Arabia's market by the middle of this month, marking the end of the kingdom's total reliance on white sugar imports mainly from the European Union.

Mohammad Ajlan, vice-president and general manager of Saudi Arabia's United Sugar Co (USC), said on Wednesday the company, the kingdom's first sugar refinery, will start receiving local purchase orders from June 7.

"The first Saudi refined sugar should be in the market from June 14," he told Reuters from the Saudi Red Sea city of Jeddah. "We are still in the commissioning period and official commercial production starts in the middle of June."

Per capita consumption of sugar in Saudi Arabia is among the world's highest at around 30 kg and total annual consumption is around 550,000 tonnes. But the total is expanding amid population growth of three to four percent a year.

The start of production of the 500,000 tonne annual capacity refinery means imports of white sugar mainly from the EU and China will drop sharply and the country of 18 million people will become a predominantly raw sugar market.
The refinery is 51 percent owned by Savola -- Saudi Arabia's biggest food group, 15 percent by Britain's Tate and Lyle Plc and the rest by Saudi sugar trading firms.
Ajlan said the refinery would produce 250,000 tonnes in 1997, which would all be sold locally.

"Our prices will be competitive and determined by international and domestic trends on weekly basis," Ajlan said. "Our aim is to meet the local needs and we will only export if there is an excess, but we don't expect to have any," he said.
He said the refinery would import a total of some 270,000 tonnes of raw sugar for 1997. It has so far received 54,000 tonnes from Australia. "We are using some of that in the commissioning process."
He said a 38,000 tonne raw sugar shipment from South Africa was expected to arrive in Jeddah between June 10 and 14.
A further shipment of 34,000 tonnes will follow in September to meet current contractual commitments, although South African industry sources said additional sales were possible.
Ajlan said USC was negotiating for more raw sugar from Australia and South Africa as well as Thailand. "Our options are open and will be according to demand and production."
The International Sugar Organization says the big Middle East import market, traditionally supplied mainly with beet from the EU, was now increasingly drawing raw sugar from other areas.

Other than USC, nearby Dubai has the new al-Khaleej plant with targeted annual capacity of 720,000 tonnes. Another Saudi firm is expected to start production at the kingdom's second white sugar producer in the next two years.
Al-Jouf Agricultural Development Co said in April it had received government approval for the 120,000 tonne factory. The company plans to produce white sugar from locally grown sugar beet.
